style: carry on from the previous verse in one line

candidates.angle: Arjuna names Krishna as the first divine being
candidates.evidence: त्वमादिदेवः (You are the first divine being)

candidates.angle: He calls him the ancient person
Krishna is the knower and the known
candidates.evidence: वेत्तासि वेद्यं च (You are the knower and the knowable)

en.intro: Carrying on from his praise of Krishna as the first maker, Arjuna now names the ancient person who is the highest refuge.
en.notice: Arjuna calls him the ancient person, the supreme person, the knower, and the knowable, saying the whole world is pervaded by him. He sees Krishna as both the one who knows and the one who is known.
en.next: He then names Krishna as the wind, fire, the moon, and the great ancestors, bowing again and again.
en.meaning: You are the first divine presence, the ancient person, the supreme refuge of this universe. You are the knower, the knowable, and the highest abode. O infinite one, the whole world is pervaded by you.

hi.intro: पहले की तरह कि आप ही आदि रचयिता हैं, अब अर्जुन उस प्राचीन पुरुष को पुकारते हैं जो सबसे ऊँचा आश्रय है।
hi.meaning: आप ही आदिदेव और पुराणपुरुष हैं तथा आप ही इस संसारके परम आश्रय हैं। आप ही सबको जाननेवाले, जाननेयोग्य और परमधाम हैं। हे अनन्तरूप, आपसे ही सम्पूर्ण संसार व्याप्त है।
hi.notice: अर्जुन उन्हें पुराण पुरुष, परम पुरुष और जानने वाले व जानने योग्य कहते हैं। वे कहते हैं कि सारा संसार उनसे ही व्याप्त है। वे कृष्ण को जानने वाले और जाने जाने वाले दोनों रूपों में देखते हैं।
hi.next: वे फिर आपको वायु, अग्नि, चंद्रमा और पितरों के रूप में देखते हैं, और बार-बार आपको प्रणाम करते हैं।

en.intro: Carrying on from his praise of Krishna as the first maker, Arjuna now names the ancient person who is the highest refuge.
en.body: You are the first divine presence, the ancient person, the supreme refuge of this universe. You are the knower, the knowable, and the highest abode. O infinite one, the whole world is pervaded by you. Arjuna calls him the ancient person, the supreme person, the knower, and the knowable, saying the whole world is pervaded by him. He sees Krishna as both the one who knows and the one who is known. He then names Krishna as the wind, fire, the moon, and the great ancestors, bowing again and again.
